claims.statement: Tom Allen beat Bill Davis in 43 rounds on Chouteau Island, St. Louis, on January 12, 1869.
claims.excerpt: resulted in a forty-three-round victory over Bill Davis, the Californian, on Chouteau Island, St. Louis, January 12, 1869.

claims.statement: After beating Davis, Tom Allen claimed the championship of America.
claims.excerpt: By beating Davis, i have earned the right to claim the championship

claims.statement: Tom Allen said he would fight any man in the country who disputed his claim, for any purse that the challenger named.
claims.excerpt: I'll give him a battle any time he wants it and for any purse that he names

claims.statement: Charlie Gallagher beat Tom Allen on Carroll Island, near St. Louis, on February 23, 1869, after three minutes of fighting.
claims.excerpt: Gallagher won + on three minutes of fighting by landing a terrific

claims.statement: Charlie Gallagher challenged Tom Allen again a few days after the McCoole fight.
claims.excerpt: A few days afterward Gallagher again challenged Allen

claims.statement: Tom Allen fought Mike McCoole for a $1,000 side bet on Boster's Island, near St. Louis, on July 15, 1869.
claims.excerpt: took on Mike McCoole in a battie on Boster's Island, near St. Louis.

claims.statement: The referee gave the fight to Mike McCoole under threat from McCoole's backers, after Allen had outfought him.
claims.excerpt: Confronted with the alternative of death or deciding in favor of a beaten warrior

claims.statement: Charlie Gallagher and Tom Allen fought a rematch on Foster's Island, near St. Louis, on August 17, 1869.
claims.excerpt: the contest was fought on Foster's Island August 17, 1869.

claims.statement: Allen battered Gallagher for eleven rounds, but Gallagher's backers cut the ropes and threatened referee Larry Wessel, who then declared Gallagher the winner.
claims.excerpt: Allen battered his rival from one side the other for cleven rounds

claims.statement: Tom Allen issued a boasting challenge that he could whip any man in the world, and Jem Mace accepted it.
claims.excerpt: issued by Allen that he could whip any manin the world

claims.statement: Jem Mace beat Tom Allen in the tenth round, after forty minutes of fighting, at Kennerville, La., in May 1870, for a side bet of $2,500 and the championship of the world.
claims.excerpt: The finish came for Allen in the tenth round—after forty minutes of fighting.

claims.statement: Tom Allen challenged Mike McCoole once more, about two years after the Mace fight, and McCoole accepted.
claims.excerpt: challenged Mike once more, He accepted and the battle

claims.excerpt: Allen beat McCoole almost to a pulp, winning in twentr- nine rOunds
